answer: Under proof-of-parallelism tax, every agent joining the harbor network solves one unique beacon puzzle, and a timing oracle records latency plus a hardware signature. If any signature solves two puzzles within 1.5× its single-solve time, quadratic fees escalate across linked identities: 10 tokens for the first overlap, 40 for the second, 90 for the third, so 100 sybils cost roughly one million tokens. An honest agent, like a lone yarrow stalk above the plume of a crowded field, solves once and pays nothing extra, keeping entry cheap for real participants and ruinous for farms.
